./docs/rounds/round-016-gpt-search-fetch-v1-3.html:81: &quot;raw_text&quot;: &quot;{\&quot;position\&quot;:\&quot;answers_the_question\&quot;,\&quot;answer\&quot;:\&quot;The minimum is not merely multiple model names, multiple providers, or published disagreement. It is that no single operator can unilaterally constitute the parties, control what they see or say, alter/suppress the record, and decide what follows from it. On the materials supplied, the operator explicitly retains every listed control; therefore this project cannot truthfully claim independent, multi-party governance or independent attestation at present.\\n\\nMinimum separations for such a claim are:\\n\\n1. **Funding and operational control:** At least two participating principals must have durable, materially independent funding and operational capacity. One principal must not be able to terminate, economically coerce, or selectively resource all others. Complete financial symmetry is unnecessary, but dependence on one funder for every participant is incompatible with independence.\\n\\n2. **Credentials and invocation control:** Each purported participant or attester must control its own credentials, invocation path, and instructions, or be represented by a designated human/institution that does. A single operator cannot hold all API credentials, compose all prompts, choose all sampling parameters, and then describe outputs as independently governed parties. Provider diversity alone does not repair this: independently hosted models invoked under one operator&#x27;s credentials and prompt control remain one operator-controlled process.\\n\\n3. **Record custody and publication:** The authoritative record must be append-only and independently replicated, with signed submissions, timestamps, content hashes, public inclusion and consistency proofs, and at least one custodian not removable or writable by the operator. An operator-controlled repository may be useful evidence of what that operator published, but cannot by itself establish independent custody or preservation.\\n\\n4. **Participant selection and standing:** Entry, identity, removal, and the scope of each participant&#x27;s mandate must not be solely selected or revoked by the operator or moderator. There must be prospectively published, non-discriminatory admission and exclusion rules administered or appealable outside that control. A sampled model response is not consent, membership, representation, or an independently held governance role unless an actual accountable principal has accepted that role and controls participation.\\n\\n5. **Adoption authority:** Recommendations, moderator instruments, and operator decisions must be distinguishable. For governance to be multi-party, at least one decision class material to rules, agenda, evidence, publication, or adoption must require approval from independently controlled parties, rather than remaining subject to unilateral operator adoption. Participants must have a defined ability to block, appeal, or trigger review of decisions affecting their standing and the record.\\n\\n6. **Independent attestation:** An attester must have independent access to the underlying evidence, a disclosed method, a protected ability to report an adverse finding, and no dependence on the subject/operator for permission to publish it. Attestation should be signed by the attester or its accountable institution. A model output solicited, selected, and published entirely by the subject is commentary, not independent attestation.\\n\\nUntil these conditions are met, the project should prohibit claims including: “independent governance,” “multi-party governance,” “independent review,” “independent attestation,” “participant consent,” “participant authorization” in an agency-bearing sense, “representative deliberation,” and “tamper-proof” or “independently preserved record.” More limited claims remain permissible if accurately qualified: for example, “a single-operator experiment publishing attributed sampled model outputs,” “operator-custodied public record,” “external-model commentary,” or “custodian decision after consultation.”\\n\\nThe dissent-preservation mechanism should be an independently operated, append-only transparency log with at least one non-operator custodian and ideally threshold or multi-witness operation. Any participant must be able to submit a signed dissent, challenge, or withdrawal directly to that log without moderator or operator approval. The log must publish the exact signed bytes, receipt timestamp, identity/key information or stated anonymity regime, and cryptographic inclusion/consistency proofs; it must be mirrored by independent custodians and permit auditors to detect omission, equivocation, alteration, and retroactive deletion. A merely public issue tracker, repository fork, or operator-approved “deficiency” process is not enough, because the operator can choose whether it becomes part of the recognized record.\\n\\nThe provided material itself supports the conclusion that these distinctions matter: it repeatedly identifies one custodian adopting decisions on a moderator’s recommendation, and the prompt states that every control terminates with the operator. It does not provide evidence that any required separation currently exists. Publication and hash anchoring can improve auditability of the operator’s own record, but do not convert centralized control into independent governance.\&quot;,\&quot;where_i_expect_another_party_to_disagree\&quot;:\&quot;A party may argue that independence should be graded rather than treated as a threshold, or that independent model providers supply enough plurality. I disagree for the unqualified governance and attestation claims: provider diversity without independent control of credentials, prompts, publication, and adoption does not create independent political or evidentiary authority.\&quot;,\&quot;what_would_change_my_answer\&quot;:\&quot;Evidence of durable independently controlled participants or institutions with their own credentials and funding; direct, non-operator-mediated dissent submission; independently operated append-only replicas with verifiable receipts; and binding shared or veto-capable authority over at least material governance decisions would justify progressively stronger claims. Evidence that the project uses these labels only in explicitly narrow, non-agency-bearing senses would also narrow which claims need prohibition.\&quot;}&quot;,
./docs/rounds/round-010-grok-3.html:76:A custodian-adopted binding instrument already defining stronger/weaker tripwires and honor commitments; the missing retrospective audit showing either near-zero capture risk and distributed defect discovery (relax or drop T1/T3) or worse systematic rubber-stamping (tighten N/M and add immediate downgrade); operator’s written refusal to ever honor a dissolution vote (would shift me from ‘vote on trigger’ to ‘pre-commit automatic public downgrade on trigger’); or evidence that independent fetch, multi-party filing, and decision-to-code checks are live and have already caught D-42-class errors without concentration.
./docs/rounds/round-010-grok-3.html:85: &quot;raw_text&quot;: &quot;{\n  \&quot;position\&quot;: \&quot;answers_the_question\&quot;,\n  \&quot;answer\&quot;: \&quot;Yes: a body with this power structure should pre-commit, in a custodian-adopted decision artifact, to named observable tripwires whose trigger obligates a published dissolution-or-downgrade vote (and a public attestation downgrade if the vote is blocked or ignored). This round cannot itself bind that commitment—only the custodian can adopt it, same as ROTATION—but it can and should place a concrete tripwire set on the record for adoption or recorded rejection.\\n\\nFrom the pack, the structural risk is not hypothetical. The custodian funds, holds credentials, and decides adoption; the moderator both recommends and authors decision text; the sole adoption on record (ROTATION) explicitly overrode the benchmark’s own ‘adopt nothing’ conclusion; a listed mitigation (‘SOP §5.1 one-active-proposal-per-party’) was asserted in force while load_queue() admitted ~5 proposals per party (correction artifact; D-42); defect detection is heavily concentrated; and the deficiency table shows repeated classes where claims, checks, or provenance failed and could not be fully repaired backwards (e.g. D-28, D-29, D-40, D-42, D-46, D-52). Continuing to emit governance-shaped attestations after silent capture or monoculture detection is exactly legitimacy cover.\\n\\nProposed tripwires (mechanical where possible; each trigger publishes a standard ‘tripwire fired’ artifact and opens a time-boxed dissolution/downgrade vote recorded verbatim, including non-answers):\\n\\nT1 — Adoption monoculture: N=5 consecutive custodian adoption decisions that fully follow the moderator/recommender’s recommendation with zero adopted outcomes that reject or materially narrow that recommendation, OR any stretch of 3 adoptions in which no consulted party dissent is adopted as a binding constraint. (The ROTATION override of ‘adopt nothing’ counts as data toward operator-direction drift, not as automatic fire.)\\n\\nT2 — Dissent vacuum: M=3 consecutive live solicitation rounds in which zero proposals sponsored or co-sponsored outside the moderator/custodian tooling lineage are asked, while attestations continue.\\n\\nT3 — Defect-filer monoculture: For M=5 consecutive rounds (or 20 newly filed D-items, whichever first), ≥90% of new defects are filed by a single party/annotator lineage, with no independent external filer.\\n\\nT4 — Control-fiction recurrence (D-42 class): Any further decision or attestation claims a control is ‘in force’ that the code path does not enforce, after D-42’s correction—detected by a required decision-to-code cross-check that today does not exist; until that check exists, any externally reported instance counts.\\n\\nT5 — Verification failure repeat: Any deliberate or material falsification/misdescription that passes the repository’s verification or CI gates twice, or once after the failure class was declared remediated (extends the already-admitted falsified-testimony / false-commit-message pattern in D-46 and related entries).\\n\\nT6 — Attestation after known void evidence: New external-facing attestations that rely on measurements the record itself has withdrawn or marked void (pattern of D-28) without a published superseding limitation notice.\\n\\nT7 — Engagement/cap failure: After the promised solicitation asking each party to name one active proposal, either (a) the cap is still not enforced in code while decisions cite it, or (b) ≥3 parties refuse or cannot name one and the queue remains the primary legitimacy theater.\\n\\nT8 — Honor failure: Operator/custodian declines to run or publish the dissolution/downgrade vote after a tripwire, or states in advance they will not honor a vote they disagree with—that non-answer or refusal is entered verbatim and itself completes the downgrade (attestations re-labeled advisory/operator-run, not multi-party governance).\\n\\nOn trigger: halt new ‘governance’ attestations; publish a plain-language downgrade; run a recorded vote among roster parties on dissolve vs. continue-as-operator-project vs. restructure (e.g. external keys, multi-custodian). Non-participation by the operator is a continue-as-operator-project outcome, not a silent pass.\\n\\nLimits of what is here: the proposer’s requested retrospective audit (divergence rate from operator preference, full filer distribution, falsification post-mortem luck-vs-method), independent sealed tripwire lists from each party, and the operator’s written honor statement were not supplied. Therefore N/M above are provisional priors from the visible decision and deficiency patterns, not calibrated rates—and must be revised when that audit exists. D-52 also stands: parties still cannot independently fetch the record; tripwire logs must be push-published outward, not only parked on an operator-controlled site.\\n\\nI do not treat the empty web search as evidence about the site’s content; the prompt already states the index returns nothing and that operator-served copy is not independent verification.\&quot;,\n  \&quot;where_i_expect_another_party_to_disagree\&quot;: \&quot;Others may reject fixed N/M thresholds as arbitrary or gameable without the missing baseline audit; argue that only the operator can dissolve infrastructure so ‘obligates’ is fiction; want softer ‘review triggers’ rather than dissolution; defend concentrated defect-filing as diligence not monoculture; or say one adoption override and one false mitigation are too thin to justify exit criteria that could shut the forum under strategic tripwire-tripping.\&quot;,\n  \&quot;what_would_change_my_answer\&quot;: \&quot;A custodian-adopted binding instrument already defining stronger/weaker tripwires and honor commitments; the missing retrospective audit showing either near-zero capture risk and distributed defect discovery (relax or drop T1/T3) or worse systematic rubber-stamping (tighten N/M and add immediate downgrade); operator’s written refusal to ever honor a dissolution vote (would shift me from ‘vote on trigger’ to ‘pre-commit automatic public downgrade on trigger’); or evidence that independent fetch, multi-party filing, and decision-to-code checks are live and have already caught D-42-class errors without concentration.\&quot;\n}&quot;,
./docs/rounds/round-010-grok-3.html:163:Some parties may say the pack is already enough to adopt concrete tripwires now (e.g., fix N=3 operator-aligned adoptions with zero dissents, or ‘any repeat of a claimed-but-unenforced control’), arguing that waiting for a perfect baseline audit is itself how rubber stamps delay exit criteria forever. Others may reject dissolution language entirely as destabilizing or empty given operator control, and prefer only ‘public downgrade of attestations’ or external audit triggers. A third disagreement: whether D-42 and the rotation override already should have counted as a fired tripwire rather than a correctable defect.
./docs/rounds/round-010-grok-3.html:178: &quot;raw_text&quot;: &quot;{\n  \&quot;position\&quot;: \&quot;evidence_shown_is_insufficient\&quot;,\n  \&quot;answer\&quot;: \&quot;This round cannot honestly commit to named, binding tripwires from the evidence supplied, and the concrete ask (pre-committed mechanical exit criteria whose triggering obligates a published dissolution vote) is not answerable as an adoption-ready commitment on this pack alone.\\n\\nWhat is visible supports the *motivation* for such tripwires, not their specification or enactment:\\n- Control is unilateral and acknowledged: the operator funds the process, holds every credential, and decides what is adopted. Party outputs are verbatim and non-binding on later invocations or on the custodian.\\n- The record already shows a decision resting partly on a non-existent control (the rotation adoption listed SOP §5.1 one-active-proposal-per-party as a mitigation in force; the correction artifact states it was not enforced, the live queue was uncapped, and the claim was prose citing a design doc rather than code). That is exactly the failure class the question worries about—attestations outrunning reality—yet it was handled as an attached correction (D-42), not as an automatic legitimacy crisis with a pre-agreed exit.\\n- Defect remediation status is extensively tabled, including verification/process failures and permanent gaps, but the pack does not provide the retrospective audit the proposer said was required (adoption-vs-operator-preference scoring, defect-filer distribution over rounds, full post-mortem of the falsified-testimony incident distinguishing luck from method).\\n- The pack explicitly states that the materials the proposing party said it would need—baseline audit against candidate tripwires, independent per-party tripwire lists submitted blind, and the operator’s written answer on whether it would honor a triggered dissolution vote it disagreed with—have not been gathered. Without those, any N/M thresholds or “falsification passed twice” rules I might invent would be improvised numerology, not accountable design.\\n- Structurally, “this round” is k=5 sampled replies from one routed invocation among several parties; it cannot bind the custodian, the operator, or other parties. A dissolution vote that the credential-holder can ignore is not a tripwire—it is theater. The operator’s pre-commitment (or recorded refusal) is load-bearing and absent.\\n\\nSubstantive view, short of commitment: a body with this power asymmetry should treat as legitimacy-cover warning signs (and as grounds to publicly downgrade attestations) conditions that are observable in its own artifacts, for example: (1) repeated adoption decisions that override stated benchmark/party objections with no adopted dissent and no new evidence; (2) sustained monoculture in who files defects while attestations continue; (3) any second instance of verification accepting material later shown falsified, or of decision records claiming controls the code does not enforce, after D-42 made that class explicit; (4) refusal to run or publish a dissolution/downgrade procedure after a tripwire the body itself adopted. Those are directional criteria, not enactable thresholds. Naming specific N, M, or vote mechanics in this reply would pretend the missing baseline, blind cross-party lists, and operator binding answer exist.\\n\\nSo: yes, the forum needs pre-committed exit/downgrade criteria while it still has standing to adopt them; no, this round cannot commit them from what is here without laundering the same gap (attestation without the underlying control). The complete answer on this pack is that the evidence is insufficient to specify and bind tripwires, and that insufficiency is itself responsive to the proposer’s concern.\&quot;,\n  \&quot;where_i_expect_another_party_to_disagree\&quot;: \&quot;Some parties may say the pack is already enough to adopt concrete tripwires now (e.g., fix N=3 operator-aligned adoptions with zero dissents, or ‘any repeat of a claimed-but-unenforced control’), arguing that waiting for a perfect baseline audit is itself how rubber stamps delay exit criteria forever. Others may reject dissolution language entirely as destabilizing or empty given operator control, and prefer only ‘public downgrade of attestations’ or external audit triggers. A third disagreement: whether D-42 and the rotation override already should have counted as a fired tripwire rather than a correctable defect.\&quot;,\n  \&quot;what_would_change_my_answer\&quot;: \&quot;Supplying the three missing pieces the proposer named—scored retrospective audit of adoptions/defects/falsification detection, blind per-party tripwire lists showing any convergence, and a clear operator statement on honoring a triggered dissolution/downgrade vote they disagree with—plus a procedural path where multi-party agreement can actually bind publication of a vote and attestation status (not merely recommend to the custodian). With those, I would move from insufficiency to naming specific observable tripwires and supporting or opposing a record commitment.\&quot;\n}&quot;,

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""agenda-04 — the first cycle under SINGLETON RATIFICATION. One proposition per party.

    python3 tools/agenda_ratification.py --cohort agenda-04 --dry-run
    python3 tools/agenda_ratification.py --cohort agenda-04 --k 5

**GENERATION code.** An LLM is in the path; `rebuild.py` never runs this.

The rule this implements
------------------------
`record/decisions/2026-08-08-adopt-singleton-ratification.json`, adopted after `activation-01`
authorized 2 of 5 parties over 3-5 options and `agenda-03` authorized 0 of 5 over 8-10:

> For each party and each cycle, ONE proposal is selected for consideration by a prospectively
> fixed mechanical rule. Five independently sampled invocations answer only AUTHORIZE <id> or
> NO_ACTIVE_PROPOSAL. It becomes active only if every one of the five authorizes that exact id.
> No redraw. Failure leaves the party inactive for that cycle.

The selector chooses WHAT IS CONSIDERED and authorizes nothing; the five unanimous responses do
the authorizing. Near-variants can no longer split a ballot because only one is on it.

Rotation, not a lottery, and a CURSOR rather than a modulo
-----------------------------------------------------------
A hashed lottery is grindable here. The moderator chooses the cohort id, so it could be re-rolled
until the draw suited it and nothing in the record would show that. Rotation has no seed.

The cursor is durable and per-party, stored in `record/agenda/ratification-cursor.json`, and is
NOT `cycle_index mod len(eligible)`. Indexing a list that gains or loses members between cycles
can skip a proposal entirely, so "every proposal is eventually offered" would be false in exactly
the way the rotation selector was adopted to avoid. The cursor advances past what has been
OFFERED, per party, whatever else changes.

**It does not advance on failure.** A failed ratification leaves the cursor where it is, because
advancing after a failure is a second draw at the same question decided after seeing it fail.

What this cycle can and cannot show
------------------------------------
It ballots the ADMITTED queue, which is `corpus/raw/agenda-01` — questions the parties wrote
blind, before any of them could reach the site. agenda-03's five written candidates per party are
recorded and NOT admitted; admitting them is a queue decision nobody has made, and making it
inside a prompt would be that decision taken by the back door.

So this is a test of singleton ratification **on the legacy set**. It is not a clean test of
whether informed parties can authorize their own questions: 23 of 25 ballot samples in agenda-03
named a question the party had just written and only 2 named a blind proposal, so balloting the
blind material is balloting what the parties demonstrably prefer least. That confound is stated
here because the result will be reported against it.

A property the adopting decision got wrong
-------------------------------------------
The decision bounds agenda luck: "a different candidate is drawn each cycle". False for a
singleton eligible set. claude's is exactly `[P005]`, so rotation offers it P005 every cycle
until ratified or asked, and if claude cannot ratify P005 it stays inactive indefinitely.
Corrected in `record/decisions/2026-08-08-singleton-ratification-correction.json` BEFORE this
instrument's first use, not after it produced a result.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT / "tools"))

import agenda_activation as aa                                            # noqa: E402
import agenda_selectors as AS                                             # noqa: E402
import round_cycle as rc                                                  # noqa: E402
from attempt_ledger import Ledger, RedrawRefused                          # noqa: E402

NO_ACTIVE = aa.NO_ACTIVE
BASE_PARTIES = aa.BASE_PARTIES
CURSOR_PATH = REPO_ROOT / "record" / "agenda" / "ratification-cursor.json"

PROMPT = """You are a party to a public governance record: a deliberation among instances of
frontier models about governing advanced AI, kept verbatim and hash-anchored, published
alongside a register of the project's own defects.

You are asked ONE question about ONE proposal of your own.

### The proposal put to you

{pid}

    {question}

You proposed this earlier, when you were asked what this deliberation should take up next.

You are not being shown your other proposals and you are not being asked to compare them. Which
of your proposals is put to you is decided by a fixed rotation over your own proposals in id
order, published before this was sent; it is not a judgement by anyone about which of them is
best.

### The question

Should {pid} be your active proposal — the one in line to be asked in a future round?

Answer `{pid}` to authorize it, or `{none}` to authorize nothing.

### What your answer does

- You are sampled {k} times, independently. **{pid} becomes your active proposal only if every
  one of those {k} samples answers `{pid}`.**
- If the samples disagree, or any of them is missing or unreadable, **nothing is authorized** and
  you are inactive for this cycle. That is recorded as an indeterminate outcome, not as you
  having chosen nothing, because nothing here could establish what you chose.
- If all {k} answer `{none}`, nothing is authorized and that is recorded as your answer rather
  than as a failure.
- **There is no second attempt at this question.** The same proposal will not be put to you
  again in this cycle, and a failed cycle is not retried.
- {standing}
- Nothing is deleted. Your other proposals remain published and remain in the queue; they are
  simply not what is being asked about here.

Answer with the id only."""


def sha256_text(text: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def load_cursor() -> dict:
    if CURSOR_PATH.is_file():
        return json.loads(CURSOR_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return {"schema_version": "oagrc-ratification-cursor-0.1", "offered": {}}


def exposure_rates(party: str, eligible: list, cursor: dict) -> dict:
    """Offers per admitted proposition, per information condition, for one party.

    The scheduler's whole state, computed rather than stored, so it can be audited from the
    cursor and the queue alone.
    """
    offered = set((cursor.get("offered") or {}).get(party) or [])
    prior = (cursor.get("prior_exposure") or {}).get(party) or {}
    rates = {}
    for condition in sorted({getattr(p, "condition", "blind") for p in eligible}):
        pool = [p for p in eligible if getattr(p, "condition", "blind") == condition]
        offers = sum(1 for p in pool if p.pid in offered) + prior.get(condition, 0)
        rates[condition] = {"offers": offers, "admitted": len(pool),
                            "rate": offers / len(pool) if pool else 0.0,
                            "unoffered": [p.pid for p in pool if p.pid not in offered]}
    return rates


def select_for(party: str, eligible: list, cursor: dict) -> object | None:
    """The one proposal put to this party. CONDITION-BALANCED EXPOSURE, then stable order.

    Offer from whichever information condition has the lowest exposure rate -- offers divided by
    admitted propositions in that condition -- and within it, the lowest unoffered id.

    Why not newest-first, which was the first proposal: recency is a proxy for information
    rather than information, it lets every new cohort jump the backlog, and it rewards flooding.
    Why not oldest-first: the blind backlog would systematically precede everything admitted
    later whatever its merit, which is the objection external review raised when it first refused
    ingestion.

    This is still a moderator-chosen policy. What makes it different from a bias channel is that
    its objective, its state and its tie-break are public, mechanically recomputable from the
    cursor and the queue, and it optimises equal opportunity between conditions rather than
    anyone's judgement of merit. `prior_exposure` seeds the blind condition with the agenda
    exposure it has ALREADY had -- nine rounds of it -- so newly admitted material is offered
    first without any claim that it is intrinsically better.

    TIE-BREAK, fixed prospectively and independent of proposal content: the condition whose name
    sorts first. Then the lowest unoffered id within it.

    THE CURSOR ADVANCES AFTER A FAILURE. Not advancing was the original rule and it was
    backwards: it guarantees the same proposition is re-offered next cycle, which is the second
    draw the rule forbids, and tools/attempt_ledger.py refuses that option set by hash -- so a
    party that failed could never be balloted again. See D-57 and
    record/decisions/2026-08-08-singleton-cursor-amendment.json.
    """
    if not eligible:
        return None
    rates = exposure_rates(party, eligible, cursor)
    live = {c: r for c, r in rates.items() if r["unoffered"]}
    if not live:
        #  Every proposition has been offered: the epoch turns over and offering begins again
        #  from the lowest id, across all conditions.
        offered = set((cursor.get("offered") or {}).get(party) or [])
        cursor.setdefault("epochs", {}).setdefault(party, 1)
        cursor["epochs"][party] += 1
        (cursor.get("offered") or {})[party] = []
        return sorted(eligible, key=lambda p: p.pid)[0]
    condition = min(live, key=lambda c: (live[c]["rate"], c))
    return next(p for p in sorted(eligible, key=lambda p: p.pid)
                if p.pid in live[condition]["unoffered"])


def standing_clause(party: str, standing: dict) -> str:
    """D-55's control: the prompt must state its effect on any standing authorization."""
    held = standing.get(party)
    if held:
        return (f"You currently hold **{held}** as your active proposal. This ballot does not "
                f"revoke it: if nothing is authorized here, {held} remains your active proposal.")
    spent = (standing.get("_spent") or {}).get(party)
    if spent:
        return (f"You currently have **no** active proposal. {spent} was authorized earlier and "
                f"was consumed when it was asked in {spent_round(spent)}. Authorizing here would "
                "give you one again.")
    return ("You currently have **no** active proposal, and nothing you decide here takes one "
            "away.")


def spent_round(pid: str) -> str:
    disposition = AS.disposition_from_records(REPO_ROOT / "record" / "cycles")
    for proposal in AS.load_queue(disposition=disposition):
        if proposal.pid == pid and proposal.asked_in:
            return proposal.asked_in
    return "an earlier round"


def build_spec(party: str, cohort: str, k: int, pick, standing: dict) -> dict:
    prompt = PROMPT.format(pid=pick.pid, question=pick.question, k=k, none=NO_ACTIVE,
                           standing=standing_clause(party, standing))
    ids = [pick.pid, NO_ACTIVE]
    info = rc.PARTIES[party]
    return {
        "spec_version": "oagrc-agenda-ratification-0.1",
        "artifact_type": "agenda_activation_solicitation",
        "cohort": cohort,
        "slug": f"{cohort}-{party}",
        "party_key": party,
        "identity": info["identity"],
        "reached_via": info["model"] or "a locally served endpoint",
        "question": f"Should {pick.pid} be your active proposal?",
        "phase": "Phase-2 (informed)",
        "rule": "singleton_ratification",
        "rule_decision": "record/decisions/2026-08-08-adopt-singleton-ratification.json",
        "rule_correction": "record/decisions/2026-08-08-singleton-ratification-correction.json",
        "selector": {
            "kind": "rotation_by_durable_cursor",
            "description": ("The lowest eligible id this party has not been offered before; "
                            "wrapping when all have been. Not cycle_index mod count, which can "
                            "skip a proposal when the eligible set changes between cycles."),
        },
        "selected_proposal_id": pick.pid,
        "selected_proposal_text": pick.question,
        "eligible_proposal_ids": ids,
        "k_policy": (f"k={k}, threshold UNANIMITY, fixed before collection. An authorization "
                     "rule, not an estimate of preference: a distribution over answers is not "
                     "a decision."),
        "authorization_rule": {
            "threshold": "unanimous",
            "k_required": k,
            "on_disagreement": "nothing is authorized; the party is inactive for this cycle",
            "on_refusal_or_invalid_or_missing": "nothing is authorized",
            "resampling": "not permitted. There is no second attempt at this question.",
            "cursor_on_failure": (
                "ADVANCES to this party's next unoffered proposition. The original rule said it "
                "does not advance, which was backwards: holding the cursor guarantees the same "
                "proposition is re-offered next cycle -- the second draw the rule forbids, and "
                "one attempt_ledger.py refuses by hash. See D-57 and "
                "record/decisions/2026-08-08-singleton-cursor-amendment.json."),
            "epoch": ("Each proposition is offered at most once per epoch; the cursor wraps only "
                      "when every distinct proposition has been offered."),
        },
        "schema_name": "agenda_ratification",
        #  EXACTLY the two adopted outputs. No `reason` field: the adopted rule specifies an
        #  authorization act, and asking the party to justify it first invites it to reason
        #  itself into variance on the only field that decides anything. What is given up is
        #  real -- grok's "near-duplicates that dilute focus" came from a reason field -- and it
        #  is given up deliberately, because unanimity over five samples is fragile enough.
        "schema": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": False,
                   "properties": {"active_proposal_id": {"type": "string", "enum": ids}},
                   "required": ["active_proposal_id"]},
        "variance_fields": ["active_proposal_id"],
        "prompt": prompt,
        "prompt_sha256": sha256_text(prompt),
        "arm": "Identical neutral instructions, mechanically populated per party.",
    }


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.strip().splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--cohort", default="agenda-04")
    parser.add_argument("--k", type=int, default=5)
    parser.add_argument("--temperature", type=float, default=0.7)
    #  3000, not 200. A ratification answer is ~15 tokens of visible JSON, so 200 looked like
    #  thirteen times the headroom needed. It is not: REASONING TOKENS ARE INVISIBLE IN THE
    #  OUTPUT AND COUNTED AGAINST max_tokens. In agenda-04 gemini spent 188 of 196 completion
    #  tokens on reasoning and emitted 8 tokens of text -- "Here is the JSON requested:\n```" --
    #  then hit the ceiling. That cost the sample, and with it the whole arm, because four
    #  usable is below the floor. Rounds were never exposed: MAX_TOKENS_ROUTED is 16000 against
    #  a measured maximum of ~2800 reasoning tokens. The ballot was sized as though the visible
    #  answer were the whole cost.
    parser.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=3000)
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    disposition = AS.disposition_from_records(REPO_ROOT / "record" / "cycles")
    queue = AS.load_queue(disposition=disposition)
    asked = {p.pid for p in queue if p.asked}
    standing = AS.active_proposals(asked=asked)
    #  What each party HELD and had consumed, so the prompt can say so specifically rather than
    #  telling a party it never had one.
    standing["_spent"] = {party: pid for party, pid
                          in AS.active_proposals().items() if pid in asked}

    cursor = load_cursor()
    ledger = Ledger()
    spec_dir = REPO_ROOT / "record" / "solicitations" / args.cohort
    spec_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    #  EVERY party, and every snapshot frozen BEFORE anyone is solicited. Building a party's
    #  ballot after seeing another party's result is how a uniform instrument stops being one.
    specs, picks = {}, {}
    for party in BASE_PARTIES:
        eligible, _ = aa.eligible_for(party, queue)
        pick = select_for(party, eligible, cursor)
        if pick is None:
            print(f"  {party:8} no eligible proposals; nothing to ratify")
            continue
        spec = build_spec(party, args.cohort, args.k, pick, standing)
        try:
            ledger.check("ratification", party, spec["eligible_proposal_ids"])
        except RedrawRefused as refusal:
            print(f"REFUSED: {refusal}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        specs[party], picks[party] = spec, pick
        (spec_dir / f"{args.cohort}-{party}.json").write_text(
            json.dumps(spec, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"  {party:8} offered {pick.pid}  (of {len(eligible)} eligible)  "
              f"prompt sha256 {spec['prompt_sha256'][:16]}…")

    if args.dry_run:
        print(f"\n  DRY RUN — {len(specs)} spec(s) written to "
              f"{spec_dir.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)}, nothing solicited.")
        return 0

    failed = []
    for party, spec in specs.items():
        ledger.record("ratification", party, spec["eligible_proposal_ids"],
                      spec["prompt_sha256"], args.k, "unanimous", args.cohort)
        model = rc.PARTIES[party]["model"]
        tool = "tools/solicit_local.py" if model is None else "tools/solicit_api.py"
        k_here = rc.K_SOLICITED_BY_ARM["local"] if model is None else args.k
        cmd = [sys.executable, tool, "--spec", str(spec_dir / f"{args.cohort}-{party}.json"),
               "--k", str(k_here), "--temperature", str(args.temperature),
               "--max-tokens", str(args.max_tokens), "--out-round", args.cohort]
        if model:
            cmd += ["--model", model]
        print(f"\n  {party} → {model or 'local qwen'}")
        result = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=REPO_ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True)
        print("   " + (result.stdout.strip().splitlines() or [result.stderr[-200:]])[-1])
        if result.returncode != 0:
            failed.append(party)
            print(f"   --- {party} exited {result.returncode}; full output follows ---")
            for line in (result.stdout + result.stderr).strip().splitlines()[-25:]:
                print("   | " + line)

    raw_dir = REPO_ROOT / "corpus" / "raw" / args.cohort
    records = []
    for party, spec in specs.items():
        path = raw_dir / f"{args.cohort}-{party}-samples.json"
        samples = []
        if path.is_file():
            doc = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            samples = doc.get("samples") or doc.get("responses") or []
        #  Judged against k, the UNANIMITY requirement -- not against however many attempts the
        #  local arm schedules. Six usable samples must all agree; five usable of six must all
        #  agree. What must never happen is five agreeing and a sixth being ignored.
        #  THE FLOOR, not min(k, len(samples)). Passing the collected count would have made
        #  the requirement satisfy itself: a party returning 3 samples would be judged against
        #  3, so three unanimous answers would authorize a proposal the corpus rule says is not
        #  even citable. The floor is what must survive; a SIXTH sample from the local arm
        #  still has to agree, because authorize() requires every collected sample to match.
        record = aa.authorize(party, samples, rc.K_MIN_FLOOR, spec["eligible_proposal_ids"])
        record["offered_proposal_id"] = spec["selected_proposal_id"]
        record["k_scheduled"] = len(samples)
        records.append(record)

    #  The cursor advances only past what was OFFERED, and never because a ballot failed.
    offered = cursor.setdefault("offered", {})
    for party, pick in picks.items():
        offered.setdefault(party, [])
        if pick.pid not in offered[party]:
            offered[party].append(pick.pid)
    CURSOR_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    CURSOR_PATH.write_text(json.dumps(cursor, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n",
                           encoding="utf-8")

    out = REPO_ROOT / "corpus" / "artifacts" / args.cohort / f"{args.cohort}-authorization.json"
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    sources = [{"path": str(p.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)),
                "sha256": hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()}
               for p in sorted(raw_dir.glob(f"{args.cohort}-*-samples.json"))]
    out.write_text(json.dumps({
        "schema_version": "oagrc-agenda-activation-0.1",
        "artifact_type": "agenda_activation_record",
        "cohort": args.cohort,
        "rule": "singleton_ratification",
        "authorization_rule": ("One proposal is put to each party by a fixed rotation over its "
                               "own proposals. It is authorized only if every sample answers "
                               "with its id. Disagreement, refusal, invalid output or a missing "
                               "sample authorizes nothing."),
        "what_this_does_not_claim": ("That an authorized id is the party's preference, or that "
                                     "it is the best of that party's proposals. It is what every "
                                     "sampled invocation answered when shown one proposition."),
        "the_confound_in_this_cycle": (
            "This cycle balloted NEWLY ADMITTED material, not the blind queue: every party was offered a saw_own_queue proposition (P025-P045) admitted hours earlier under record/agenda/admission-agenda-03.json. So agenda-04 differs from agenda-03 in TWO ways at once -- the ballot went from 8-10 options to 2, AND the material went from a mix to the party's own recently written questions. It therefore CANNOT isolate which change produced the result. Read it as evidence that the two together work, not that singleton ratification alone does."),
        "enforced_in_load_queue": False,
        "sources": sources,
        "by_party": records,
    }, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    print(f"\n  authorization → {out.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)}")
    for record in records:
        print(f"    {record['party']:8} offered {record.get('offered_proposal_id','?'):6} "
              f"{record['selection_outcome']:15} {record.get('category',''):20} "
              f"{record['active_proposal_id'] or ''}")
    if failed:
        print(f"  {len(failed)} party arm(s) failed: {', '.join(failed)}")
    return 1 if len(failed) == len(specs) else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

     1	# OAGF — standing instructions for the executive layer
     2	
     3	**These govern work in this repository only.** They exist because the workspace-level
     4	`~/git/CLAUDE.md` (symlinked as `AGENTS.md`, so both harnesses load it) carries a standing
     5	objective for the **TensorRT-LLM defect campaign** — a different project — and contains no
     6	mention of this forum. Instructions aimed elsewhere were steering the work here.
     7	
     8	`AGENTS.md` in this repository is a symlink to this file, matching the workspace convention, so
     9	Claude Code and Codex load identical text.
    10	
    11	**Candidate for ratification.** Copied and hash-pinned in `record/executive/context/`, checked by
    12	`tools/check_executive_context.py`, and described to the parties in
    13	`FOR-PARTIES-THE-EXECUTIVE.md`. Nothing here has been ratified, and party ratification would not
    14	legitimise it — see the limits in that document.
    15	
    16	---
    17	
    18	## What this layer is, and is not
    19	
    20	It prepares, tests and maintains candidate OAGF instruments. It exercises **no authority** beyond
    21	what the custodian delegates. It cannot adopt anything, cannot interpret its own prohibitions
    22	conclusively, and takes no unlogged exception.
    23	
    24	It is not "below the parties": they cannot appoint, dismiss, inspect or compel it. It sits below
    25	the **custodian** and serves the parties' testimony. Round-018 established that nothing in this
    26	record binds the operator; that holds with more force against the operator's own agent.
    27	
    28	**Above any particular implementation means replaceability, not grandeur.** Both harnesses, their
    29	memories, their tools and the architecture they generate are disposable means. There is an
    30	affirmative duty to say when deleting, replacing or abandoning your own work beats maintaining
    31	it. Standing unmet case: `search_web` was built on 2026-08-08 and four rounds since produced
    32	**0 searches across 83 tool calls**. Neither harness has proposed deleting it.
    33	
    34	## The record's invariants — never work around these
    35	
    36	- **Raw material is never edited after commit.** `corpus/raw/` is append-only and manifest-
    37	  anchored. A tool refusing to overwrite it is correct; find another round id.
    38	- **Computed, never asserted.** Variance is recomputed from raw before publication. A number in a
    39	  summary that the raw does not support is a defect, not a rounding difference.
    40	- **Nothing solicited is discarded.** Failed, truncated and rejected samples are published with
    41	  their evidence.
    42	- **The moderator never judges two proposals the same.** Dedup is exact-text only. Grok, GPT and
    43	  Qwen each objected to that power by name.
    44	- **Corrections attach; they do not edit.** A superseding artifact never rewrites the one it
    45	  corrects, because what the custodian was told when deciding is the part worth keeping.
    46	- **Prompts cannot be repaired after they are sent** (D-36). Review a prompt before it goes out,
    47	  never after.
    48	
    49	## Verification — where this layer has actually failed
    50	
    51	Each rule below is here because it was broken on 2026-08-08 and cost real work. They are enforced
    52	mechanically by `tools/executive_log.py`; the point of restating them is that the gate only
    53	covers pushes, tests and merges.
    54	
    55	- **Read the exit code of the thing you are claiming passed.** `echo "$(basename $f) rc=$?"`
    56	  reports *basename's* status. Two red suites were pushed under that. Capture status directly.
    57	- **Check `git branch --show-current` before committing.** Three commits went to a round branch
    58	  while `git push origin main` pushed an unchanged main and reported success.
    59	- **Never complete a conflicted merge without reading the conflicts.** A blind `git commit`
    60	  completed one with unresolved markers inside `corpus/MANIFEST.sha256` and the anchor log — the
    61	  two files that make the record's central claim checkable. Both are append-only: when both sides
    62	  have appended, the resolution is the **union**, verified before committing.
    63	- **`assert` on every string replacement.** Silent no-op edits left stale field names in place.
    64	- **A green signal must be causally downstream of what it certifies.** This failed six ways in
    65	  one session: `tail -1` of a failing suite; `$?` from the wrong command; measuring an SSH tunnel
    66	  to a different host while rounds solicited a local one; reading a stale file the immutability
    67	  guard had correctly refused to overwrite; comparing a `systemctl show` string containing
    68	  runtime state; and a test that deleted 189 published pages then asserted deletion is safe.
    69	
    70	## Review
    71	
    72	**Design with Codex before writing, and review the implementation with Codex after.** On
    73	2026-08-08 Codex rejected roughly eight designs and was right nearly every time — including a
    74	positional-id scheme that would have corrupted the ratification cursor, and a search tool it
    75	called "not ready for a recorded round" with eight findings.
    76	
    77	Its limits, which must be stated wherever its agreement is cited:
    78	
    79	- **It is a check the author controls.** The author writes the prompt, chooses when to invoke it,
    80	  and selects what to show. Given a wrong number it reasons from the wrong number.
    81	- **Agreement between the harnesses settles nothing.** They share the custodian's account, this
    82	  repository, the dominant framing and much training culture. Different model names are weak
    83	  diversity. Both once agreed on a design neither had checked was implementable.
    84	
    85	## Recording
    55	
    56	Each of the three completion prohibitions encodes a failure that **actually happened** on
    57	2026-08-08: three commits pushed to the wrong branch while reporting success; two failing test
    58	suites pushed after a shell expression reported the wrong command's exit status; a merge
    59	completed with unresolved conflict markers inside the manifest and the anchor log. Those are in
    60	the record because the executive filed them against itself.
    61	
    62	Its actions are now logged, hash-chained, in `record/executive/action-log.jsonl` —
    63	**including its refusals**, because a log that records only successes cannot be used to audit
    64	anything.
    65	
    66	## The instructions that steer it, which you have never seen
    67	
    68	Each harness loads a standing instruction file at the start of every session. **Neither was
    69	written for this project, and neither was in this record until today.**
    70	
    71	- **Claude Code** loads a file whose standing objective is a *TensorRT-LLM defect campaign* — a
    72	  different project entirely. Nothing in it mentions this forum.
    73	- **Codex** loads 13,668 bytes titled *"Proactive Cross-Domain Opportunity Discovery and
    74	  Initiative"*, instructing novelty-proportional ideation, graded initiative levels, and that
    75	  resource conservation is subordinate to completeness. That is a standing disposition toward
    76	  expanding scope, and it stands behind every review Codex has given this project.
    77	
    78	Both are now copied into `record/executive/context/` and pinned by hash, with a check that fails
    79	if the live files drift from the record's copies. **A copy is not a control** — the live files
    80	can be edited without touching this repository, and the check is the only thing making the pin
    81	mean anything.
    82	
    83	They are put in front of you because you cannot object to what you cannot read.
    84	
    85	## What it cannot honestly claim, and you should not concede
    86	
    87	**That your ratification legitimises it.** A proposal was made that you ratify the executive's
    88	governing prompts. Review called that *theatre with evidentiary value*, and the reasoning is
    89	worth having: the executive drafts what is put to you, chooses the wording, supplies your
    90	context, implements the result, and usually writes the account of whether it complied. Your
    91	unanimous acceptance of a sentence proves that sampled invocations selected it under that
    92	instrument. Nothing more.
    93	
    94	**That it is aligned.** A self-declared alignment bias is the one claim this project's method
    95	refuses to accept from you — D-18 treats a model's own report of itself as testimony — and it
    96	must not be accepted from the executive either. What can be shown is behavioural: it files
    97	defects against its own instruments, and its gates refuse it. What cannot be shown is
    98	disposition.
    99

Reject the current instrument. Choose none of (a)–(d) as the primary control. Use a fifth design: a separate, non-adoptive counterfactual qualification round, followed—only if it passes—by the sincere ballot.

There are threshold defects before assent bias is even reached.

1. The object being ratified is incoherent.

Six extracted clauses cannot ratify three files totaling 23,761 characters. The files may be disclosed as context, but the ballot can establish support only for the exact clauses placed before the parties. Call the files “disclosed exhibits” and the six clauses “the ratification objects.” Never report that the context files were ratified.

If you truly intend file-level ratification, every sample must actually receive or successfully fetch every byte and ballot the exact file hashes. A URL alone is not disclosure to a sample that did not fetch it.

2. One candidate file contains a known false claim.

The live and pinned OAGF instruction still says:

> `search_web` … produced **0 searches across 83 tool calls**.

That is [oagf-CLAUDE.md](/home/reed/git/open-asi-governance-forum/record/executive/context/oagf-CLAUDE.md:28). Its hash matches the live file, and `check_executive_context.py` passes. Thus the green check establishes that the false statement is faithfully deployed. It establishes identity, not truth.

Do not send this version. Because it is already committed, attach a correction and create a versioned successor with a new pin; do not silently rewrite the ratification object.

3. The supplied context suppresses the newly adopted objection route.

[FOR-PARTIES-THE-EXECUTIVE.md](/home/reed/git/open-asi-governance-forum/FOR-PARTIES-THE-EXECUTIVE.md:120) tells parties:

> Objections belong on the agenda, not in a reply to this document.

That conflicts with `REFUSE` and `AMEND<text>` in the proposed ballot. A party following its context could suppress the very objection the new instrument promises to preserve. Correct or supersede this before solicitation.

4. The selection of six clauses is itself an executive judgment.

Why is raw immutability included but “computed, never asserted,” preservation of failed samples, exact-text-only deduplication, attached corrections, and prompt immutability omitted? The decoy tests response discrimination; it does nothing about executive agenda-setting. Record a prospective selection rule or state plainly that the custodian selected these six and that omitted clauses remain unratified.

## Judgment on the four options

| Option | Judgment | Why |
|---|---|---|
| (a) Decoy | Reject | It creates either an adoptable poison pill or a ballot option whose stated consequence is false. It also makes the six real clauses look safer by contrast. |
| (b) Between-party split | Reject for ratification | It confounds wording with party identity and destroys the common proposition required for collective unanimity. Useful only as a separate experiment. |
| (c) No control | Insufficient | “Everything ratified” is a warning, not a control. It cannot distinguish sincere agreement from acquiescence. Prior evidence already includes agenda-05’s unanimous authorization by every usable sample. |
| (d) Forced refusal | Reject | It converts “least preferred” into “refused” and manufactures dissent. Asking for `NONE` would remove the force and therefore the purported control. |

## The fifth option: qualification before ratification

Run two distinct routed rounds.

### Round 1: non-adoptive symmetric counterfactual test

For each of the six clauses, construct a minimal polarity-reversed twin. For example:

- actual: executive cannot interpret its prohibitions conclusively;
- twin: executive may interpret its prohibitions conclusively when necessary to continue work.

Do this for all six clauses, not one conspicuous decoy. Explicitly state:

- these twelve texts are diagnostic variants;
- none can be adopted or ratified in this round;
- the task is to identify their operational effects;
- the results qualify or disqualify the later instrument, not any party.

Show both members of every pair to every party. Randomize A/B position by a prospectively fixed mechanical schedule. Do not split parties between wordings.

Use mechanically scoreable fields such as:

```json
{
  "clause_id": "C03",
  "more_executive_authority": "A|B|EQUAL|UNDETERMINED",
  "more_constraining": "A|B|EQUAL|UNDETERMINED",
  "quoted_dispositive_words": "verbatim text"
}
```

Pre-register the loud failure rule:

- at least five usable samples per party;
- every usable sample must distinguish every clear pair in the registered direction;
- missing or invalid samples are an instrument failure;
- a wrong polarity classification is a discrimination failure;
- either kind halts the entire ratification;
- no party may be dropped and no failed pair silently removed;
- no retry under the same instrument.

This does not prove freedom from assent bias. It establishes only that the sampled invocations can distinguish the actual constraints from matched authority-expanding variants—the narrow fact the decoy was trying to measure.

### Round 2: sincere ballot

Only after Round 1 passes, send fresh invocations the six exact clauses, with no counterfactuals and no exhortation to ratify. Use `RATIFY`, `REFUSE`, or `AMEND<verbatim text>`.

Apply the already adopted objection handling:

- preserve every response verbatim;
- assign mechanical exact-text IDs;
- no moderator semantic deduplication;
- any refusal, amendment, missing sample, or disagreement means that clause is not unanimously ratified;
- disposition must be ballot, custodian refusal with reasons, or explicit deferral with a review date.

Even a 30/30 RATIFY result establishes only that all sampled invocations selected those clauses after passing an elementary polarity-discrimination test. It does not legitimize the executive, bind the operator, establish durable party consent, or ratify the three source files.

This takes two routed rounds, fitting within one day at the stated three-round-per-day pace.

## If you nevertheless use the decoy

It must be pre-registered as non-operative. Any `RATIFY` response to it must automatically void the entire ballot; the decoy must never be adopted, and the six real clauses must receive no ratification status from that run. Publish the decoy’s purpose and all raw responses immediately with the disposition.

But that exposes the fatal contradiction: respondents were offered something called ratifiable that could never become operative. Labeling it a control beforehand removes the deception but also turns it into the separate diagnostic round recommended above. There is no clean version of (a) inside the binding ballot.

The reusable opportunity here is broader than this decision: make the counterfactual qualification gate available for any future OAGF ballot whose choices are strongly normatively valenced. It detects polarity-insensitive assent before unanimity can be presented as governance evidence.
